subject: R homeworks: tools for sending/publishing R(md) files?

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: R homeworks: tools for sending/publishing R(md) files?
parts:
Hi

We are using R for a course, and want students to send their homeworks in Rmd format. Ideally, the Rmd files could be sent by students to a centralised repository, kept inaccessible for a while (to prevent copying from others), then made accessible to all to present results during discussion section. 

Which tool, workflow would you recommend? One possibility would be to ask students to send through Canvas, or Rpubs, then for us to centralize, and push into github or alike. That's the easiest on the student side, but can require quite a few manual steps on the TA side. 

An alternative is for students to have their own github account, then do pull requests. This is more complicated on student side, and I am not sure how to handle the "undisclosed period", as ?

Any ides or suggestions for other worflows? 

Thanks!

Matthieu

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R homeworks: tools for sending/publishing R(md) files?
parts: Some thoughts below

On Wed, Jan 10, 2018 at 6:35 PM, Matthieu Stigler <mmst...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
Hi

We are using R for a course, and want students to send their homeworks in Rmd format. Ideally, the Rmd files could be sent by students to a centralised repository, kept inaccessible for a while (to prevent copying from others), then made accessible to all to present results during discussion section.

In an old school CS class, the way they do this is with an account on a shared server and a script that copies (and checks) the assignment from a student's directory to a TAs. eg: https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs107/submit.html If you're working on shared servers or everyone in the class can somehow copy the script to a remote, this might be an option.

An issue like this (many student-submitted files to process) on the legacy learning-tech site at davis (smartsite) led me to write some scripts (https://github.com/ashander/smartersite). These processed batch-downloads from the site. It wasn't perfect and required one batch download per assignment but it helped. If Canvas has some batch download feature a little scripting could help lessen the TA overhead.

Which tool, workflow would you recommend? One possibility would be to ask students to send through Canvas, or Rpubs, then for us to centralize, and push into github or alike. That's the easiest on the student side, but can require quite a few manual steps on the TA side.
Rpubs is public right? how would the workflow work there? would pre-submission inaccesibilty rely on assuming students didn't know each other's Rpubs accounts?
An alternative is for students to have their own github account, then do pull requests. This is more complicated on student side, and I am not sure how to handle the "undisclosed period", as ?

This https://classroom.github.com is a thing, which I've never used, or looked at (only heard of on twitter). I'd guess it has features to handle submission of assignments that are not immediately visible to all students. Let us know if it works!

Any ides or suggestions for other worflows? 

Thanks!

Matthieu

messages.author: 91fcdff1323a6831
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R homeworks: tools for sending/publishing R(md) files?
parts:
Just to chime in, we are using github classrooms for an R course, which has been great, however, at the moment it's mainly been a one way usage. We create a repository which Github Classroom then uses to create a repository for each student, appending their username to the repo name. I don't think it is currently functional for folks to submit things back in the way that you are describing (without some significant overhead burden on the student and instructors...branching, merge/merge conflicts, pull requests, general mayhem).

That being said, any reason not to submit content via a google form? You can now attach files via a google form, which could go into a folder that is only shared with TAs/instructors. After you've reviewed the Rmd's, you could move the files to a new shared folder on Google Drive which the entire class would have access to. The google form would allow you to track who submits what and when, ensuring that submissions happen by a specific deadline. That also eliminates the need for folks to need to know Git (unless that's a component you are planning on teaching).  If not that, you could use Box in a similar way...we've had success doing this for submissions to a student magazine (see our submission form here on the Aggie Brickyard site

Good luck.

Ryan

messages.author: f14d4c9d01f43388
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: R homeworks: tools for sending/publishing R(md) files?
parts:
Hi Jaime, Michael and Ryan

Thanks for the inputs! To answer first the few questions, students are expected to have little to no knowledge of R and git(hub), but that's first year PhD class. And yes, the idea of Rpubs was that you would need to know the colleagues pseudo to access their files, so not the most secure indeed. 

The github classroom tool seems interesting. Do I understand well that it sets up ready github repos for the students (who still need to create github accounts)? Which automatically will push to a repository we control? That seems pretty nice. We could have that repo private (though that costs a few $), and eventually push later on to a public git repo, so that everyone can see everyone's homeworks. That's the two steps we need, we don't need a push-back system actually. 

But otherwise, yes we could simply ask to use the Canvas assignment system, which seems indeed to be bulk downloadable. Then have a simple script compiling the Rmd, and pushing these to a pubic github repo, might be the easiest. 

Thanks for the valuable comments!

Matthieu
